newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian ministers in dispute over oil refineries.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian ministers in dispute over oil refineries.

text.p: Oil minister Dan Etete on Thursday refuted remarks by his finance counterpart that funds voted to repair Nigerian oil refineries had yielded no tangible results.
"There has been no extra-budgetary allocation to the (state-run oil company) NNPC," Etete said in a statement.

Finance minister Anthony Ani said in a public lecture in the northern Kaduna city last weekend that "Despite the huge amount allocated for the refineries, we have found that they have not been repaired, the result of which is persistent shortage of fuel in Nigeria, the world's sixth largest producer of oil."
According to him, $440 million and $295 million were allocated to the Nigerian National Petroleum Corp (NNPC) in 1995 and 1996, respectively, for projects including refinery repairs.

But Etete disputed this, calling Ani's remarks "a deliberate falsehood with intent to incite the Nigerian masses and pitch the international community against not only the ministry of petroluem resources and the NNPC but to embarrass and discredit the present administration."
Despite having four refineries and being one of the leading crude oil producers, Nigeria frequently suffers from bouts of fuel shortage.
Lagos, the nation's commercial hub is currently crippled by a shortage of fuel that has stranded thousands of motorists.
"Government is aware of the present fuel situation and while regretting the inconviniences to the public, is addressing the matter with a view to finding a lasting solution," Etete said.
Nigeria's four refineries have a combined capacity of 445,000 barrels of crude oil daily but produce at a fraction of their capacity due to deteriorating facilities.
Etete and Ani, who both come from the oil-producing southeast of Nigeria have long been at odds over economic policy including oil, Nigeria's lifeblood.
